turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr Ellison, I've done your obs. Blood pressure is 138 over 82, pulse is 76. Doctor won't be long.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ta. It's the elbow I'm here about, not the blood pressure.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): G'day, I'm Dr Patel. Have a seat. What's been going on with you?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Outside of the right elbow. Hurts like someone's stuck a hot nail in it.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm Karen, his wife. He nearly didn't come, which is typical.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long's that been going, and what sets it off?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, six weeks. Well, actually, I don't know, doctor, maybe a touch longer, but yeah about six weeks. Lifting a cuppa sets it off, and the tools are worse.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Still on the tools with it?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah I'm a carpenter, framing and decks. I reckon I've overdone it on a job out at Werribee. Even a full mug and I pull a face.
[SEG0010] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He dropped the drill last Tuesday. The grip on that side is shot.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, grip's weak. I don't know, doctor, might just be me letting go 'cause it hurts. Not all day.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any pins and needles, or does the hand go dead?
[SEG0013] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If this is about his ears, he can't hear himself think in the workshop, the radio and the nail gun flat out the whole...
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not his hearing. The hand. Any numbness?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No pins and needles, hand's not numb. Feet are fine as well but you didn't ask, and the noise is just the job, I'm not deaf.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever over these six weeks?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Some nights I get home feeling like a wrung-out rag, but that's being buggered from work, not a temperature.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any cough, or shortness of breath? Just checking I'm not missing something else.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough. Breathing's good. I don't know, doctor, nothing doing there.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Has your weight gone up or down?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. I don't know, doctor. Karen reckons the jeans sit looser. I haven't been on any scales, so maybe, maybe not.
[SEG0022] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I said baggy. I didn't say he was wasting away, so don't you write weight loss.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): I won't. Too muddy to call. What are you taking for the elbow?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Ibuprofen for the elbow. Nurofen from the chemist, the 400 milligram tablets.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): How often do you actually take them?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Two times a day, sometimes three. Meant to be with food. Some arvos I skip the middle dose. I don't know, doctor, I'm slack with it.
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And half the time it's on an empty stomach in the ute. I've seen the blister pack.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Empty stomach is the bit I don't love. Any heartburn on it, or black stools?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No heartburn. No black stools. Gut's been sweet.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines? Aspirin, ibuprofen, rash or swelling?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't know of any, doctor. Never been told I've got one.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Other regular medicines, even a vitamin?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Only a green bottle, fish something. I don't know the name. Karen buys it.
[SEG0034] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Don't ask me the brand. Chemist Warehouse, green bottle, fishy capsules, one most mornings. That's the lot.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll note an unnamed fish capsule and leave it. Ever had a scan for this elbow?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): An ultrasound. They said it was borderline, something about the tendon. Last year, or, err, the year before, I don't know, doctor. They never gave me a number.
[SEG0037] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It was the imaging place in Footscray. Nobody rang to say it was actually bad. Just that borderline word.

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Old ultrasound, called borderline by them, no figure, and the date's fuzzy. I won't treat that as a measurement we can use. Thinking aloud, pain on the outer elbow with grip and lifting a cup for about six weeks is the usual story for lateral epicondylitis.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me feel it. Tender right on the lateral epicondyle. Pushing your wrist up against my hand copies the pain. No swelling, and the elbow straightens and bends fully.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Yep. That's the spot. Ow.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): So my working impression is lateral epicondylitis, tennis elbow. Pattern plus the exam, not a fresh scan, and not set in stone. No injection today.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. I hate needles. What do I do then?

[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep the ibuprofen at 400 milligrams, with food, not in the ute on an empty stomach, and you can ease off once it settles. Get a tennis elbow brace from the chemist, the strap just under the sore spot. I'll refer you to physio for the slow wrist-lowering exercises.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back and see me in six weeks. If it's still stopping you on the tools we might talk about a cortisone injection then, but only if the physio hasn't done the job. Not before.
[SEG0045] person_1 (NURSE): If you both stop at the desk I'll book the physio referral and the six-week review. They're going in today, not a maybe.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Righto. We'll give it a crack. I don't know if the boss'll like the time off, but Karen'll nag me there.

spec.situation: Painter or carpenter with outer elbow pain for six weeks, worse lifting a cup; takes ibuprofen; physio and brace advice; no injection yet.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

bad.reason: Weak grip is reported, but certainty is not certain; patient says it might be due to pain and not all day.
bad.text: weak grip (category=musculoskeletal, status=present, temporality=current, body_site=right hand, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Completed ultrasound is supported, but transcript does not say it was requested by the patient.
bad.text: elbow ultrasound (type=imaging, status=completed, requested_by=patient, indication=elbow pain)

bad.reason: Conditional cortisone injection is supported, but it was discussed by doctor, not requested by doctor.
bad.text: cortisone injection (type=other, status=conditional, requested_by=doctor, indication=pain still limiting work after physiotherapy)

omissions.text: Grip weakness is intermittent/not present all day, and the patient was unsure whether it is true weakness versus letting go because of pain.

Weight change was specifically asked about and not established: patient had not been weighed and said maybe/maybe not; wife said jeans were baggier but not true weight loss, and doctor agreed it was too unclear to call.
No injection today was explicitly stated.
Previous elbow ultrasound result was described as 'borderline', with something about the tendon, from an imaging place in Footscray; doctor said it should not be treated as a usable measurement.
Physio referral and six-week review were to be booked that day ('they're going in today, not a maybe').
